claim: A reference — the thing a manifest lists or a human types — has up to four parts.
evidence: spec/modules/vibe-registry/PROP-008-qualified-naming.md:82  ##PKGREF-GRAMMAR **Decision.** The pkgref grammar gains an optional `group` segment and makes the `kind` prefix
searched: The four parts are literally the four fields of the host's PackageRef struct — kind, group, name, version — with the same optionality: kind and group are Option, name and version are not (version defaults to VersionSpec::Latest rather than being absent). PROP-008 ##PKGREF-GRAMMAR states the same production. This is one of the tightest grammar-to-type matches in the package.

claim: An optional type tag.
searched: Optional in the type (Option<PackageKind>) and optional in the parser (split_once(':') falls through to None when absent). Both directions are tested: parse_short_bare asserts kind == None for `wal`, and parse_short_with_kind asserts kind == Some(PackageKind::Flow) for `flow:wal`. The tag's value set is closed — PackageKind has five variants (flow, feat, stack, tool, mcp) and `parse_rejects_bad_kind` pins that an unknown tag errors, which is narrower than this file's `kind := ident`.

claim: An optional group qualifier.
searched: Optional in the type and in the parser, exactly as stated. Worth recording the scope of 'optional', because the host narrows it: the doc comment on the field says None occurs 'only for an unresolved short CLI ref; a manifest pkgref is always qualified', and `vibe uninstall` rejects a group-less ref outright. So the group is optional in the GRAMMAR and mandatory in every persisted position — which is what §storage later says.

claim: A mandatory name.
searched: Mandatory in the type — PackageName, not Option<PackageName> — and enforced at the parse seam: parse_rejects_bad_name asserts that `org.vibevm/` (group with an empty name) is an error, and PackageRef::parse errors on empty input. The one place the host's grammar is NARROWER than this document's. `ref-grammar.md`'s EBNF gives `name := ( lower | digit | "_" | "-" )+`; the host's `validate_package_name` in `crates/vibe-core/src/package_ref.rs` is kebab-case only — no underscore, no leading or trailing hyphen, no doubled hyphen — and its test `name_rejects_invalid` in `crates/vibe-core/src/package_ref/tests.rs` asserts `"with_underscore"` is rejected. The `group` production matches: `Group::parse` accepts `a`–`z`, `0`–`9`, `_`, `-` per dot-separated segment, and `group_accepts_valid` accepts `org.vibevm_internal`. So the underscore is legal in a host group and illegal in a host name.

claim: An optional version requirement.
searched: Optional and modelled explicitly: VersionSpec::Latest is the absent case ('No version given — resolve to the latest stable'), and the parser splits on '@' with None falling through to Latest. The 'requirement' word is accurate in the host — VersionSpec::Req wraps semver::VersionReq, and parse_bare_semver_is_caret_per_cargo pins that a bare `0.3.0` means caret, i.e. a requirement rather than a pin, matching this file's own io.acme/logger@^2.1 example.

claim: Three axes, three separators: the type tag, the group and the version each attach with a different delimiter — ':' then '/' then '@' — so the parser never has to guess which axis a token belongs to.
evidence: spec/modules/vibe-registry/PROP-008-qualified-naming.md:88  ##PKGREF-SEPARATOR The `group`↔`name` separator is `/` (`:` is taken by `kind`, `@` by version). @impl/done
searched: The strongest single match in this file: PackageRef::parse is three successive split_once calls on '@', then ':', then '/', with no lookahead, no backtracking and no ambiguity resolution — which is precisely 'the parser never has to guess which axis a token belongs to'. PROP-008 ##PKGREF-SEPARATOR gives the same reason for the same choice ('The group↔name separator is / (: is taken by kind, @ by version)').

claim: The specific delimiter characters are a design choice; the load-bearing rule is that the three axes stay lexically distinct.
evidence: spec/modules/vibe-registry/PROP-008-qualified-naming.md:113  - ##JOINER-UNDERSCORE `naming = "fqdn"` maps a pkgref to the repository name `<group>_<name>`
spec/common/PROP-029-fully-qualified-addresses.md:26  - ##CARRIER-REPO-SWAP The flat repo-name carrier swaps `/`→`_` because GitHub / GitVerse names allow only
searched: The host proves the point by varying the character while keeping the axes distinct: PROP-008 ##JOINER-UNDERSCORE swaps the group↔name joiner from '/' to '_' for repository names because a repo name cannot contain '/', and picks '_' precisely because it is 'the one character in neither the group nor the name, so the coordinate stays algorithmically splittable' — distinctness preserved, character changed. PROP-029 ##CARRIER-REPO-SWAP records the same swap as a carrier rule. The design record's ##fork-separator shows the choice being made rather than assumed.

claim: Pick three delimiters that do not collide with your version syntax and never overload one.
evidence: spec/modules/vibe-registry/PROP-008-qualified-naming.md:113  - ##JOINER-UNDERSCORE `naming = "fqdn"` maps a pkgref to the repository name `<group>_<name>`
searched: The host made exactly this mistake-avoidance call and recorded the near-miss: the design record's ##fork-separator says npm-scope (@org/) was rejected as a group separator 'because @ doubling with version would confuse' — an overload of '@' across two axes, rejected for the reason this fact gives. ##JOINER-UNDERSCORE makes the same argument against '.' for repo names: 'A dot would be ambiguous — groups are dotted reverse-DNS, so <group>.<name> hides the boundary.'
